query: Which method can be used for the presence of ferromagnetic ground states, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Measuring the magnetic hysteresis at low temperature using a SQUID magnetometer can reveal the presence of a ferromagnetic ground state in high‐entropy alloys such as AlCoFeNi. In a ferromagnetic material, spontaneous alignment of magnetic moments produces a characteristic hysteresis loop (with nonzero remanence and coercivity) even in the absence of an applied field.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoFeNi high‐entropy alloy (with a continuous phase that supports strong exchange interactions among ferromagnetic elements like Co)
generation.intervention: Cool the specimen to cryogenic temperatures (e.g., 77 K) and perform magnetic hysteresis measurements using SQUID magnetometry
generation.conditions: Measurement at low temperatures to minimize thermal agitation; use of a zero-field-cooled protocol initially to detect spontaneous magnetization
generation.structural_mediator: The intrinsic atomic-scale chemical ordering (e.g., formation of B2 or BCC phases) that facilitates strong magnetic exchange interactions among constituent ferromagnetic atoms
generation.mechanism: Ferromagnetic ground states occur when the magnetic exchange interactions among elements like Co overcome thermal fluctuations, resulting in spontaneous magnetization. SQUID magnetometry is sensitive enough to detect the resulting hysteresis loop features—a nonzero remanence and measurable coercive field—even if the overall magnetic moment is modest.
generation.predicted_outcome: The as-cast AlCoFeNi alloy will exhibit a clear hysteresis loop with nonzero remanent magnetization and coercivity at 77 K, confirming the ferromagnetic ground state. In contrast, an alloy where a fraction of Co is replaced by antiferromagnetic elements (e.g., Cr) will show a significantly reduced hysteresis signature.
generation.baseline: A reference sample (e.g., AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi) with partial substitution of ferromagnetic Co by antiferromagnetic Cr should display minimal remanence and a near-linear magnetization curve at low temperatures.
generation.boundary: Results will depend on alloy processing, phase homogeneity, and the precise distribution of magnetic elements; measurement sensitivity is crucial since nanoscale segregation or competing phases might mask magnetic signals.
generation.uncertainty: Variations in microstructural features (such as local chemical ordering) and potential phase segregations may complicate the interpretation of the magnetic measurements, making it challenging to quantitate the spontaneous magnetization precisely.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two specimens: one of the as-cast AlCoFeNi alloy and a second with partial Co substitution by Cr (e.g., AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi). Cool both specimens to 77 K and measure their magnetic hysteresis loops using a SQUID magnetometer.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If both specimens exhibit similar hysteresis loops with comparable Ms, Mr, and Hc values (i.e., if the anticipated reduction in magnetic parameters upon Co substitution is not observed), then the method would not reliably indicate the presence of a ferromagnetic ground state, and the hypothesis would be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, combined with annealing temperature, influence the hierarchical phase decomposition, microhardness, and magnetic properties in AlCoFeNi-based high entropy alloys?. System: AlCoFeNi and AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi (near-equiatomic HEAs). Processing: Arc melting of elemental pellets (99.9% purity) under argon atmosphere, followed by isothermal annealing at 600 °C and 1000 °C for 15 h and water quenching. Test conditions: Annealing at 600 °C/15 h and 1000 °C/15 h; characterization via SEM, TEM, APT, EBSD, Vickers microhardness, and magnetic measurements (Ms, Hc). Findings: AlCoFeNi annealed at 1000 °C forms a single ordered B2 phase with a microhardness of 406 VHN, saturation magnetization (Ms) of 111.6 emu/g, and coercivity (Hc) of 4.3 Oe.; AlCoFeNi annealed at 600 °C decomposes into a B2 matrix and fine Fe-Co rich BCC precipitates, increasing microhardness to 474 VHN and Hc to 14.5 Oe while reducing Ms to 99.8 emu/g.; Substituting 50% Co with Cr in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi induces phase separation into B2 + BCC even at 1000 °C, with Ms dropping to 42.2 emu/g and Hc rising to 39.4 Oe.; AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi anneal
